selection_reason: user-controlled token ID -> creates upload stream -> handles arbitrary file uploads with potential path traversal
source_summary: Token ID is randomly generated (Random.id()) and not user-controlled. HTTP POST request body data flows directly to the upload stream.
sink_summary: Creates file upload stream to path '/var/sandstorm/backups/{token._id}' via sandstormBackend.uploadBackup(). FileUploadStream writes uploaded data directly to filesystem.
guard_summary: No authentication/authorization on upload route. No path traversal validation in uploadBackup implementation. FileUploadStream class implementation details unknown.
risk_pattern: Unvalidated token ID used directly in filesystem path construction enables path traversal if token ID contains '../' sequences, allowing arbitrary file overwrite.
context_summary: Route accepts POST requests to /uploadBackup, creates random token, opens upload stream using token ID as path component, streams request data to filesystem.
unresolved_facts: FileUploadStream implementation details and any internal path validation

hypotheses.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
hypotheses.fit_reason: Token ID used directly in filesystem path construction without path traversal validation. Even though token is random, if Random.id() can generate '../' sequences, arbitrary file write is possible.
Upload route has no authentication/authorization, allowing direct POST requests to upload files without any access control checks.
Direct HTTP-to-filesystem write without proper security controls could indicate backdoor-like functionality for arbitrary file uploads.

hypotheses.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
hypotheses.fit_reason: File upload mechanism may follow symlinks or other file system links if token ID manipulation creates them, leading to unintended resource access.
